answers.question: What does my plan look like over the next few months?
answers.text:
Your long-term plan runs from Monday, August 31 to Sunday, November 22, covering 12 weeks in 10 phases. You are currently in week 1 of the Base phase, which lasts from Monday, August 31 through Sunday, September 6. The next phase begins Monday, September 7. Your plan is built around your recent average of 95.5 min.

Here is the phase-by-phase outline:
- Base: Monday, August 31 to Sunday, September 6 (1 week). Use this opening week to establish easy runs and regular walks as the foundation for steady fat loss.
- Build: Monday, September 7 to Sunday, September 20 (2 weeks). Build your aerobic base while keeping the effort relaxed and the movement frequent.
- Recovery: Monday, September 21 to Sunday, September 27 (1 week). Step back this week so your body can absorb the work while you keep moving gently.
- Base: Monday, September 28 to Sunday, October 4 (1 week). Restore full-body strength while keeping easy running and walking part of your routine.
- Build: Monday, October 5 to Sunday, October 18 (2 weeks). Introduce walk-run variety to increase movement without adding unnecessary strain.
- Recovery: Monday, October 19 to Sunday, October 25 (1 week). Prioritize recovery with easy walks and light movement so you are ready for the next block.
- Maintain: Monday, October 26 to Sunday, November 1 (1 week). Maintain the running rhythm you have built and keep walking part of your week.
- Build: Monday, November 2 to Sunday, November 8 (1 week). Refresh your training stimulus with gentle run variations and ongoing walking.
- Maintain: Monday, November 9 to Sunday, November 15 (1 week). Hold a stable running routine while keeping the calorie balance moving in the right direction.
- Recovery: Monday, November 16 to Sunday, November 22 (1 week). Close this block with easy movement and a reset before the next check-in.

And the week-by-week key sessions:
- Week 1, starting Monday, August 31 (Base): key session Easy (run). Use this opening week to establish easy runs and regular walks as the foundation for steady fat loss.
- Week 2, starting Monday, September 7 (Build): key session Run/walk (run). Build your aerobic base while keeping the effort relaxed and the movement frequent.
- Week 3, starting Monday, September 14 (Build): key session Long (run). Expand your running comfort with controlled efforts and consistent walking support.
- Week 4, starting Monday, September 21 (Recovery): key session Recovery (walk). Step back this week so your body can absorb the work while you keep moving gently.
- Week 5, starting Monday, September 28 (Base): key session Strength (strength). Restore full-body strength while keeping easy running and walking part of your routine.
- Week 6, starting Monday, October 5 (Build): key session Run/walk (run). Introduce walk-run variety to increase movement without adding unnecessary strain.
- Week 7, starting Monday, October 12 (Build): key session Long (run). Deepen your running endurance with steady sessions and continued energy balance.
- Week 8, starting Monday, October 19 (Recovery): key session Recovery (walk). Prioritize recovery with easy walks and light movement so you are ready for the next block.
- Week 9, starting Monday, October 26 (Maintain): key session Easy (run). Maintain the running rhythm you have built and keep walking part of your week.
- Week 10, starting Monday, November 2 (Build): key session Intervals (run). Refresh your training stimulus with gentle run variations and ongoing walking.
- Week 11, starting Monday, November 9 (Maintain): key session Easy (run). Hold a stable running routine while keeping the calorie balance moving in the right direction.
- Week 12, starting Monday, November 16 (Recovery): key session Recovery (walk). Close this block with easy movement and a reset before the next check-in.

answers.text: Over the period from Sun Aug 2 to Mon Aug 31, your average daily step count was 10,599 steps, which is 9.69% higher than your baseline average of 9,662 steps. Your average daily active energy burned was 373 kcal, compared to a baseline of 362 kcal, a 3.17% change. Your average daily exercise time was 1 h 04 m, up 28.93% from the baseline of 49 m. Walking/running distance averaged 5.24 miles per day, versus 4.64 miles at baseline, a 12.75% increase. These figures indicate you have been quite active, with your recent averages exceeding your earlier baseline across all these measures.
